name: Undifferentiated Carcinoma of Liver and Intrahepatic Biliary Tract

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Histopathological and Immunohistochemical Diagnostic Criteria for Undifferentiated Hepatic Carcinoma

criteria.description: Presence of undifferentiated malignant epithelial cells lacking glandular or squamous differentiation on liver biopsy
Positive staining for cytokeratins (CK7, CK19) with absence of markers for hepatocellular differentiation (e.g., HepPar-1 negative)
Radiologic evidence of a mass lesion in liver or intrahepatic biliary tract with heterogeneous enhancement and absence of typical hepatocellular carcinoma features
Exclusion of other primary liver tumors and metastatic carcinomas by clinical and pathological correlation

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation of undifferentiated carcinoma cells with supportive immunohistochemical profile and exclusion of other tumor types
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires multidisciplinary evaluation including pathology, radiology, and clinical correlation.

pathognomonic.notes: Enlarged liver due to tumor mass

pathognomonic.symptomName: Obstructive jaundice due to intrahepatic bile duct involvement
searchTerms: yellow skin from liver bile obstruction
low energy due to liver issues
itchy skin due to liver problem
abdominal swelling due to liver pressure

laboratory: Elevated serum bilirubin and alkaline phosphatase
Mild to moderate elevation of transaminases (AST, ALT)
imaging: Contrast-enhanced CT or MRI showing heterogeneous liver mass with irregular margins
Intrahepatic bile duct dilatation proximal to tumor
Absence of typical vascular invasion seen in hepatocellular carcinoma
genetic: No consistent genetic mutations identified; occasional TP53 mutations reported
Lack of typical hepatocellular carcinoma molecular markers
other: Immunohistochemistry positive for cytokeratins CK7 and CK19

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of hepatocellular differentiation markers (HepPar-1 positive)
Typical vascular invasion pattern on imaging
CK7 and CK19 positive but with more differentiated morphology
Slower progression and different radiologic features
Immunohistochemical profile inconsistent with primary liver tumor

redFlags: Rapidly enlarging liver mass with obstructive jaundice
Failure to respond to standard hepatocellular carcinoma treatments
Presence of systemic symptoms such as unexplained weight loss and fever
references: Brunt EM, et al. WHO Classification of Tumours of the Digestive System, 5th Edition, 2019.
Sia D, et al. Molecular classification of hepatocellular carcinoma: implications for targeted therapy. Nat Rev Gastroenterol Hepatol. 2017.
Orphanet Report on Undifferentiated Carcinoma of Liver and Intrahepatic Biliary Tract, ORPHA:424970.
